Answer: A) Packets filled with hashish  
Reason: The ovoid opaque area at C6–C7 on the lateral neck radiograph (Figure 7) shows a smooth, well-defined ovoid shape with homogeneous high density—classic for “body packing” with hashish, which is typically compressed into dense, ovoid packets; cocaine/heroin packets are usually more irregular or less uniformly dense, and methamphetamine is rarely packed in this form.
